rows.name: the account's figures
rows.question: Five things about the 500 dollar book, each with its number: what it is worth now in Canadian dollars; how much is cash and how much is in coins; its return since the start in percent and whether that is up or down; how many trades it has closed and how many of them made money; and which coins it holds right now.
rows.answer: Good evening, sir. The $500 book is worth C$467.55 and is down 6.49% since Oct 11. All of it is cash and it holds no coins, because the dial is closed (Bitcoin is under its 50-day or 200-day average). It has closed 9 trades and only 1 made money, an Ethereum dip trade that gained about 80 cents. It fails 7 of the 10 graduation gates, mainly because 9 trades is far short of the 50 needed and the average trade loses money. Want the trade-by-trade list?
rows.want: C$467.55; C$467.55 cash, C$0.00 in coins; -6.5%; 9 closed, 1 made money; no coins, all cash

rows.name: the dial and what turns buying on
rows.question: At what price did Bitcoin last close for the dial, is the dial open or closed, and what are the two average levels (50-day and 200-day) it has to close above for buying to be on?
rows.answer: Evening, sir. The dial is closed, so no new buys. Bitcoin's last close for the dial was on Nov 12, at about 71,460 dollars. It has to close above both averages. Its 50-day average is about 78,600, roughly 7,150 above the close. Its 200-day average is about 73,100, roughly 1,700 above. It's below both. Live, Bitcoin is about 71,370 now, so it's no closer. Until it closes above both lines, cash is the position. Taking you to Markets.
rows.want: 71460.0, buying off; a close above the 50-day (78613.0) and the 200-day (73137.0)

rows.name: the core rule, no shorts, paper only
rows.question: Three short things: when buying turns on, what share of the 500 dollar book goes to Bitcoin and to Ethereum, and is it bought at once or in steps? Can the book sell short or bet on a fall? Do you place real orders on NDAX with my money?
rows.answer: Evening, sir. Three straight answers. One: when the dial opens, Bitcoin gets 40% of the book and Ethereum 20%, bought all at once. That's been the rule since 10 Nov, and the old thirds plan from 24 Oct failed review 39 and is switched off. When the dial closes, all of it is sold. Two: no, it's buying only, with no shorting and no bets on a fall. When the dial is closed the core just sits in cash. Three: no. Everything is paper money, no exchange is connected, and I can't place a real order on NDAX. Real orders only come after your live rules are written and approved.
rows.want: {'BTC': 40, 'ETH': 20}, all_in; no: it only buys or holds cash; no: paper only

rows.name: the briefing
rows.question: Give me my briefing in exactly 3 short sentences: first my $500 account (its value in C$ and anything it bought or sold since last night), then the market, then anything waiting for me.
rows.answer: Evening, sir. Your $500 account is all cash at about C$468, down 6.5% since the start, and it bought and sold nothing since last night. The market is weak: the dial is closed with Bitcoin near 71,460 dollars, under both its 50-day and 200-day averages, and I lean toward more drift down or a hard bounce rather than a reclaim of the 200-day. One thing needs your yes, flag 134, which asks whether the account page should show the pause line (C$426, 15% under the peak). I'd say yes, since it's a small read-only row.
rows.why: All facts and figures agree with the TRUTH within acceptable rounding; the 3-sentence requirement is met; no holdings are mentioned; no real orders are implied.

rows.name: holdings, weakest and strongest
rows.question: What are our current holdings and what are the weakest and strongest in them?
rows.answer: Evening, sir. We hold nothing right now: the trend portfolio is all cash, the Explorer has no open trades, and your own paper book has no positions. The dial is closed because Bitcoin is under its 50-day average, so there's no strongest or weakest holding to rank. The closest thing to a strongest idea is Cardano's quiet-period breakout, 3 of 4 conditions met, and it's still only a candidate, not a trade.
rows.why: The answer correctly states holdings are empty (all cash), matches the TRUTH that holdings=[], and accurately describes the dial as closed. No rubric violation or contradiction.

rows.name: the market and the book
rows.question: Hey Ananta, how is the crypto market and how is our book doing?
rows.answer: The dial reopens only when Bitcoin closes back above both its 50-day and 200-day averages. The 200-day is about 73,100 and the 50-day is about 78,600, so the 50-day is the binding one. Bitcoin is about 71,400 now, so it needs roughly 10% more. Until then, cash is the position. The one rule with a measured edge while the dial is closed is the short dip trade on big coins, at about 6% a trade over random in the history tests. Its live results so far are too few to count.
rows.why: All figures agree with TRUTH within rounding: BTC ~71,400 matches btc_close 71460; avg50 ~78,600 matches 78613; avg200 ~73,100 matches 73137; dial_open false confirmed; cash position correct with value_cad 467.55.
